problems.quote: Efficiency η = 1 − T_C/T_H (always 1)
problems.problem: Carnot efficiency is always less than 1 (since T_C > 0), not equal to 1.
problems.correction: Efficiency η = 1 − T_C/T_H (always < 1)
problems.verifierReason: Carnot efficiency <1 because Tc>0; correction accurate.

problems.quote: industrial belt stretching from Mumbai to Kolkata along the coast
problems.problem: No such continuous coastal industrial belt exists; major industrial corridors are Delhi-Mumbai, Amritsar-Kolkata, etc.
problems.correction: industrial corridors like Delhi-Mumbai and Amritsar-Kolkata
problems.verifierReason: No continuous coastal Mumbai-Kolkata industrial belt exists; DMIC and AKIC are designated inland corridors.

problems.quote: crossed 35 % in the 2021 Census
problems.problem: The 2021 Census has not been conducted; the 2011 Census recorded urban population at 31.16%.
problems.correction: was 31.16% in the 2011 Census
problems.verifierReason: 2021 Census postponed indefinitely; 2011 Census recorded urban population at 31.16%.

problems.quote: Pseudomonas species degrade hydrocarbons — used in Exxon Valdez, Deepwater Horizon
problems.problem: Pseudomonas species were not deliberately applied in the Exxon Valdez or Deepwater Horizon cleanups; bioremediation relied on biostimulation of indigenous microbes, not seeding of Pseudomonas.
problems.correction: Pseudomonas species degrade hydrocarbons — involved in natural attenuation after oil spills like Exxon Valdez and Deepwater Horizon
problems.verifierReason: Original implies deliberate seeding; correction correctly states role in natural attenuation.

problems.quote: USDA‑APHIS “Am I Regulated?” process evaluates whether a plant or animal product contains a plant pest component
problems.problem: USDA-APHIS 'Am I Regulated?' process only evaluates plant products, not animal products; animal gene-editing regulation falls under FDA CVM.
problems.correction: USDA‑APHIS “Am I Regulated?” process evaluates whether a plant product contains a plant pest component
problems.verifierReason: APHIS 'Am I Regulated?' applies only to plants, not animals; animal gene editing is under FDA CVM.

problems.quote: Bioinformatic tools such as TEBreak, RetroSeq, or custom pipelines align reads to a combined reference of host genome plus transgene construct
problems.problem: TEBreak and RetroSeq are tools for transposable element insertion detection, not standard for transgene integration site analysis.
problems.correction: Bioinformatic tools such as VISPA2, ISMapper, or custom pipelines align reads to a combined reference of host genome plus transgene construct
problems.verifierReason: TEBreak/RetroSeq detect transposable elements, not transgene integration; VISPA2/ISMapper are standard for vector integration sites.

problems.quote: The term was coined by Augustin Pyramus de Candolle , who is called the Father of Taxonomy.
problems.problem: Augustin Pyramus de Candolle coined the term 'taxonomy', but he is not called the Father of Taxonomy; that title belongs to Carl Linnaeus.
problems.correction: The term was coined by Augustin Pyramus de Candolle.
problems.verifierReason: De Candolle coined 'taxonomy' but Linnaeus is the Father of Taxonomy; correction removes false title.

problems.quote: Smallest living cells (0.1-0.3 m).
problems.problem: The unit 'm' (meters) is incorrect; Mycoplasma size is 0.1-0.3 micrometers (µm).
problems.correction: Smallest living cells (0.1-0.3 µm).
problems.verifierReason: 0.1-0.3 m is 10-30 cm, impossibly large for cells; Mycoplasma are 0.1-0.3 µm.

problems.quote: The provision was abrogated on 5 August 2019 by a Presidential Order CO 272 and the J&K Reorganisation Act 2019, followed by a parliamentary resolution under Article 370(3).
problems.problem: The J&K Reorganisation Act did not abrogate Article 370; it bifurcated the state after abrogation. The parliamentary resolution under Article 370(3) was part of the abrogation process, not after the Reorganisation Act.
problems.correction: The provision was abrogated on 5–6 August 2019 by Presidential Orders CO 272 and CO 273 and a parliamentary resolution under Article 370(3); the J&K Reorganisation Act 2019 later bifurcated the state.
problems.verifierReason: Original misstates sequence: Reorganisation Act didn't abrogate Art 370; resolution preceded Act; misses CO 273.

problems.quote: Article 371A (inserted in 1962 when Nagaland was formed)
problems.problem: Nagaland was formed as a state in 1963, not 1962. The amendment was passed in 1962 in anticipation of statehood.
problems.correction: Article 371A (inserted in 1962, before Nagaland's formation in 1963)
problems.verifierReason: Original wrongly states Nagaland formed in 1962; statehood was 1 Dec 1963 per State of Nagaland Act.

problems.quote: Hyderabad (Telangana) — directly elected Mayor
problems.problem: The Mayor of Hyderabad is indirectly elected by the councilors, not directly elected by the people.
problems.correction: Hyderabad (Telangana) — Mayor elected by councilors
problems.verifierReason: Hyderabad Mayor is indirectly elected by corporators under Telangana Municipalities Act

problems.quote: The 74th Amendment recommended the Nagarpalika Bill 1992 which provided for a directly elected Mayor with a fixed 5-year term
problems.problem: The 74th Amendment (1992) does not mandate a directly elected Mayor; it leaves the manner of election of the Chairperson/Mayor to state legislatures. The Nagarpalika Bill became the Amendment, not a separate recommendation.
problems.correction: The 74th Amendment leaves the manner of Mayor's election to state legislatures
problems.verifierReason: 74th Amendment (Art 243R) leaves Mayor election mode to states; Nagarpalika Bill became the Amendment

problems.quote: Gram Sabha has ownership of minor forest produce
problems.problem: PESA (1996) gives the Gram Sabha the power to manage minor forest produce, not ownership. Ownership rights were later conferred by the Forest Rights Act, 2006.
problems.correction: Gram Sabha has the power to manage minor forest produce
problems.verifierReason: PESA 1996 gives management power; FRA 2006 confers ownership rights over minor forest produce

problems.quote: The Supreme Court in A.K. Roy v. Union of India (1981) held that residuary power includes power to legislate on matters like prevention of detention
problems.problem: The case was decided in 1982, not 1981. The Court held that preventive detention falls under Entry 3 of the Concurrent List, not under residuary power.
problems.correction: The Supreme Court in A.K. Roy v. Union of India (1982) held preventive detention is under Concurrent List
problems.verifierReason: Case decided 1982; Court placed preventive detention under Concurrent List Entry 3, not residuary power

problems.quote: In September 2025, the government reduced the number of GST slabs from six to three (0%, 5%, 18%, with a 40% luxury rate), eliminating the 12% and 28% slabs.
problems.problem: No such GST slab reduction occurred in September 2025; as of 2024 GST retains five slabs (0%, 5%, 12%, 18%, 28%) plus cess.
problems.correction: As of 2024, GST retains five slabs (0%, 5%, 12%, 18%, 28%) plus cess.
problems.verifierReason: No GST slab reduction in Sep 2025; 5 slabs + cess remain as of 2024.

problems.quote: The National Anti-Profiteering Authority (NAA) was dissolved, with its functions transferred to the Competition Commission of India.
problems.problem: The NAA was dissolved in 2022, not as part of a 2025 reform.
problems.correction: The NAA was dissolved in 2022, with functions transferred to the Competition Commission of India.
problems.verifierReason: NAA dissolved Nov 2022, functions to CCI; not a 2025 reform.

problems.quote: The Commission submitted its report in 1987 with 247 recommendations.
problems.problem: The Sarkaria Commission submitted its report in 1988, not 1987.
problems.correction: The Commission submitted its report in 1988 with 247 recommendations.
problems.verifierReason: Sarkaria Commission report submitted Jan 1988, not 1987.

problems.quote: Performance-based grants — GST compensation linked to reforms
problems.problem: GST compensation is a statutory guarantee based on revenue shortfall, not a performance-based grant linked to reforms.
problems.correction: Performance-based grants — e.g., grants linked to reforms, not GST compensation
problems.verifierReason: GST compensation is statutory guarantee, not performance-based grant.

problems.quote: Removed the provision that the President can promulgate ordinances during emergency without being laid before Parliament
problems.problem: The 44th Amendment did not remove such a provision; it removed the 38th Amendment's clause making the President's satisfaction final and conclusive.
problems.correction: Removed the provision making the President's satisfaction final and conclusive (38th Amendment)
problems.verifierReason: 44th Amendment removed 'final and conclusive' clause, not ordinance-laying rule.

problems.quote: India's 1962 emergency was declared on this ground (India-China War).
problems.problem: The 1962 emergency was proclaimed on the ground of 'external aggression', not 'war'.
problems.correction: India's 1962 emergency was declared on the ground of external aggression.
problems.verifierReason: 1962 Emergency proclaimed on 'external aggression', not 'war'.

problems.quote: The 1971 emergency was initially declared on this ground due to the Bangladesh Liberation War.
problems.problem: The 1971 emergency was proclaimed on the ground of 'war' (India-Pakistan War), not 'external aggression'.
problems.correction: The 1971 emergency was declared on the ground of war (India-Pakistan War).
problems.verifierReason: 1971 Emergency proclaimed on 'war' (Indo-Pak), not 'external aggression'.

problems.quote: struck down Clause (5) of Article 368 (inserted by 42nd Amendment) which barred judicial review of constitutional amendments
problems.problem: Clause (5) of Article 368 did not bar judicial review; Clause (4) did. The Court struck down both clauses, but the description incorrectly attributes the judicial review bar to Clause (5).
problems.correction: struck down Clause (4) of Article 368 (inserted by 42nd Amendment) which barred judicial review of constitutional amendments
problems.verifierReason: Original misattributes judicial review bar to Clause 5; Clause 4 barred review. Correction accurate.

problems.quote: However, the 44th Amendment explicitly made the satisfaction subject to judicial review
problems.problem: The 44th Amendment did not explicitly state that the President's satisfaction is subject to judicial review; it introduced procedural safeguards (written Cabinet advice, parliamentary approval). Judicial review was affirmed by the Supreme Court in Minerva Mills (1980).
problems.correction: However, the 44th Amendment added procedural safeguards; judicial review was affirmed in Minerva Mills (1980)
problems.verifierReason: 44th Amendment added procedural safeguards, not explicit judicial review; Minerva Mills affirmed review. Correction correct.

problems.quote: Dealt with the removal of the Governor of Uttarakhand by the newly elected UPA government in 2009
problems.problem: The UPA government was newly elected in 2004, not 2009. The case (B.P. Singhal v. Union of India, 2010) concerned the removal of Governors in 2004.
problems.correction: Dealt with the removal of the Governor of Uttarakhand by the newly elected UPA government in 2004
problems.verifierReason: UPA first elected 2004; case concerned 2004 removals. Correction fixes year.

problems.quote: internal disturbance removed as ground for Art 19 suspension
problems.problem: The 44th Amendment removed "internal disturbance" as a ground for proclaiming Emergency under Article 352, not specifically as a ground for Article 19 suspension.
problems.correction: internal disturbance removed as ground for Emergency proclamation (Art 352)
problems.verifierReason: Original quote misstates mechanism: 'internal disturbance' was ground for Art 352 proclamation, not direct ground for Art 19 suspension. Correction accurately reflects 44th Amendment change to Art 352
